subject: Geography
stem: The Equatorial Low Pressure Belt is also known as:
solution: The equatorial low pressure belt is the classic belt of calms because air motion there is largely vertical rather than horizontal. Its traditional name is the Doldrums. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt is associated with ascending air throughout the year?
solution: Intense insolation at the equator heats the air all year, so air rises continuously there. Only the equatorial low has ascending air throughout the year. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: The Subtropical High Pressure Belt is located approximately at:
solution: The subtropical high pressure belt is centred near 30 to 35 degrees north and south. Of the ranges offered, 30 to 40 degrees is the one that contains it. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt is responsible for the origin of Trade Winds?
solution: Trade winds blow from the subtropical high pressure belt towards the equatorial low. Their source region is therefore the subtropical high. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: The Polar High Pressure Belt exists due to:
solution: The poles receive extremely slanting solar rays, so the air is very cold and dense and settles, giving high pressure. The cause is low temperature, making this a thermally induced belt. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following belts is thermally induced?
solution: Standard texts state that the equatorial low and the polar high are both thermally induced, while the subtropical high and subpolar low are dynamically induced. This question is DEFECTIVE because options C and D are both correct; the equatorial low is the more canonical example so C is the best pick. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Two options are correct: the Equatorial Low (keyed) and the Polar High are BOTH thermally induced; only the Subtropical High and Temperate Low are dynamically induced.

subject: Geography
stem: The Horse Latitudes are associated with:
solution: The horse latitudes lie in the subtropical high belt where air is descending and the surface winds are feeble and variable. That means calm winds with subsiding air. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt migrates seasonally due to the apparent movement of the Sun?
solution: The equatorial low, marked by the ITCZ, follows the overhead sun and shifts north in June and south in December. Its seasonal migration is the standard example of a belt moving with the apparent movement of the sun. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: The belt of westerlies originates from which pressure belt?
solution: Westerlies blow polewards out of the subtropical high towards the subpolar low. Their source belt is the subtropical high. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt is also known as the Subpolar Low Pressure Belt?
solution: The belt near 60 degrees north and south is called both the temperate low and the subpolar low pressure belt. The two names refer to the same belt. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: The Temperate Low Pressure Belt is formed mainly due to:
optC: Convergence of warm and cold air masses
solution: The subpolar or temperate low is a zone where warm westerlies meet cold polar easterlies along the polar front, forcing air to rise. This convergence of contrasting air masses is the main cause, and Q25 of this same paper states it explicitly. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following pressure belts is dynamically induced?
solution: The equatorial low and polar high are thermally induced, whereas the subtropical high is produced by subsidence of air converging aloft, that is dynamically. Only the subtropical high is a dynamic belt among the options, so All of the above fails. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: At which latitude are calm conditions most frequently observed?
solution: Both the equatorial belt and the subtropical belt are belts of calms, so the discriminator is the word most frequently. At about 30 degrees the descending limb of the Hadley cell gives persistently light and variable winds under clear skies, which is why sailors named it the horse latitudes. The equatorial doldrums are calm at the surface but are broken repeatedly by convectional thunderstorms, so calm conditions are less consistently observed there. Note this paper's Q47 uses Belt of Calms as a NAME for the doldrums; this question instead asks where calm is most often found. Matches option B.
reviewNote: 0 degrees (doldrums) is the belt of calms, but 30 degrees (horse latitudes) is also calm; options are not mutually exclusive.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt plays a major role in desert formation?
solution: Descending and warming air in the subtropical high suppresses condensation and produces the great hot deserts. This belt is the key control on desert formation. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: The ITCZ is associated with which pressure belt?
solution: The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone is the trough where the trade winds of the two hemispheres meet, and it coincides with the equatorial low pressure belt. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: Why are pressure belts not perfectly horizontal?
optB: Uneven distribution of land and sea
solution: If the earth had a uniform surface the belts would be continuous rings, but land heats and cools faster than water, so the belts are broken into cells and bend. The uneven distribution of land and sea is the cause. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which belt is absent in the Southern Hemisphere in a well-defined manner?
solution: Textbooks note the temperate or subpolar low appears as well marked named cells such as the Icelandic and Aleutian lows in the north, with no comparable set of cells in the south. The wording is loose, since the southern belts are in fact more continuous and regular than the northern ones, so confidence is LOW. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Loosely worded: the southern subpolar trough is arguably MORE regular than its northern counterpart.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following is correct regarding Polar High Pressure Belts?
solution: Cold dense air sinks over the poles and then spreads outwards at the surface as the polar easterlies. High pressure means divergence, not convergence or rainfall. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt is associated with frequent cyclonic activity?
solution: The temperate or subpolar low along the polar front is the birthplace of temperate cyclones, which travel eastwards with the westerlies. Cyclonic activity is most frequent there. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
solution: Equatorial low has ascending not descending air, the polar high is anticyclonic not cyclonic, and the temperate low is stormy not calm. Only the pairing of the subtropical high with the origin of the trade winds is right. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which pressure belt is located along the equator and is characterized by rising warm air?
solution: The belt lying along the equator with warm rising air is the equatorial low pressure belt. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: The Subtropical High Pressure Belts are found approximately at:
solution: The subtropical highs sit near 30 degrees in each hemisphere. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: What causes the formation of the Equatorial Low Pressure Belt?
solution: The sun is nearly overhead at the equator all year, so intense heating expands the air and makes it rise, leaving low pressure at the surface. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Deserts like Sahara and Arabian are associated with which belt?
solution: The Sahara and the Arabian desert lie near 20 to 30 degrees north under the subsiding limb of the Hadley cell, that is the subtropical high. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: The Subpolar Low Pressure Belt is mainly formed due to:
optB: Convergence of westerlies and polar easterlies
solution: Near 60 degrees the warm westerlies meet the cold polar easterlies, the warm air is forced to rise along the polar front and pressure falls. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Polar High Pressure Belts result from:
solution: Extremely low polar temperatures make the air cold and dense so that it subsides, producing high pressure at the surface. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which belt is known as Doldrums?
solution: Doldrums is the old sailing term for the calm equatorial low pressure belt. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Air pressure in belts is influenced by:
solution: The belts arise from thermal contrasts between equator and poles together with the dynamic effects of the rotation of the earth. Ocean currents, relief and volcanism are at most local modifiers. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: The Icelandic Low is an example of:
solution: The Icelandic Low is a semi permanent cell of the subpolar low pressure belt in the North Atlantic near 60 degrees north. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Subtropical highs cause:
solution: Subsiding air in a subtropical high warms adiabatically and its relative humidity falls, so clouds cannot form. The result is clear skies and dry weather, and it is not literally windless everywhere. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: How many major pressure belts exist on Earth?
solution: There are seven belts, namely one equatorial low, two subtropical highs, two subpolar lows and two polar highs. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Pressure decreases with:
solution: Pressure is the weight of the air column above, so it falls as one climbs and the column shortens and thins. Pressure decreases with altitude. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Trade winds originate from:
solution: Trade winds blow from the subtropical high to the equatorial low, so option A names the correct pair of belts but prints the direction backwards, while option B actually describes the polar easterlies. Treating the printed direction as a source slip, A is the only option naming the right pair of belts. Matches option A.
reviewNote: No option is correct as printed. Trade winds blow FROM the Subtropical High TO the Equatorial Low; option (a) names the right pair of belts but prints the direction reversed.

subject: Geography
stem: Which belt has calm winds and thunderstorms?
solution: The doldrums combine feeble surface winds with strong convectional uplift, so calm conditions alternate with towering thunderstorms. That is the equatorial low. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Aleutian Low is located in:
solution: The Aleutian Low is the subpolar low cell of the North Pacific, near 60 degrees north off the Aleutian Islands. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: High pressure belts are associated with:
solution: High pressure means subsiding air, which warms and dries and prevents cloud formation. So high pressure belts bring clear sunny skies. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: The shift of pressure belts occurs due to:
solution: The tilt of the axis of the earth produces the apparent movement of the sun, which in turn produces the seasonal temperature changes that drag the belts north and south. Both stated causes are parts of one chain, so both are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Westerlies blow between:
solution: Westerlies occupy the zone between the subtropical high and the subpolar low, that is between about 30 and 60 degrees in each hemisphere. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Normal sea-level pressure is:
solution: Standard mean sea level pressure is 1013.25 millibars, equal to 760 millimetres of mercury or one atmosphere. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Coriolis force affects pressure belts by:
solution: The Coriolis force does no heating and no lifting; it only turns moving air to the right in the north and to the left in the south. Its effect on the belts is to deflect the winds flowing between them. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements about atmospheric pressure:
1. It is the force exerted by the weight of the Earth's atmosphere on unit area.
2. Atmospheric pressure decreases with increase in altitude due to decreasing air density.
3. Earth's rotation creates centrifugal force maximum at equator, contributing to Equatorial Low.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is the definition of atmospheric pressure. Statement 2 is correct: air density and the overlying column both fall with height, so pressure falls with altitude. Statement 3 follows the standard Indian-syllabus treatment, which credits the centrifugal effect of the Earth's rotation, greatest at the equator, as a CONTRIBUTING cause of the equatorial low alongside intense solar heating - the two are taught together rather than as rivals. All three statements are therefore correct. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Statement 3 credits the Equatorial Low to centrifugal force, which sits oddly with this paper's own Q6/Q23 (thermally induced / intense solar heating).

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following places in India experiences the highest atmospheric pressure during winter due to its high altitude and cold temperature?
solution: Only Leh is both high in altitude and very cold in winter, so B is unmistakably the intended answer and it is defensible if pressure is reduced to sea level. The stem is nevertheless faulty as printed, because actual station pressure falls with altitude, so Leh records the lowest and not the highest pressure. Matches option B.
reviewNote: The stem's stated reason is self-refuting: high altitude LOWERS station pressure (Leh, ~3500 m, reads ~650 mb). Leh is recoverable only as a winter cold-core high on sea-level-reduced pressure.

subject: Geography
stem: The places having equal atmospheric pressure on weather maps are connected by:
solution: Isobars join places of equal pressure, while isotherms join equal temperature, isohyets equal rainfall and isohalines equal salinity. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Horse latitudes lie within which of the following atmospheric pressure belts?
solution: The horse latitudes are the calm subsiding zone near 30 degrees, which is the subtropical high pressure belt. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Semantic duplicate of bank row e4d3de0b...

subject: Geography
stem: Logically, continually falling air pressure at a place indicates:
optA: Advent of fine and settled weather
optB: Approach of unsettled and stormy weather
solution: Falling pressure means air is being removed from the column and is rising, which brings cloud, wind and rain, so it signals unsettled and stormy weather. Fine settled weather and an anticyclone both go with rising pressure. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding global pressure belts:
1. Equatorial Low (0°-5° N/S) results from intense solar heating causing air convection.
2. Subtropical High (30°-35° N/S) forms due to sinking air from Hadley Cell divergence.
3. Polar High (85°-90° N/S) arises from cold, dense sinking air due to slanting solar rays.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Convectional heating at the equator, subsidence from the diverging upper limb of the Hadley cell near 30 degrees, and cold dense sinking air at the poles due to very slanting rays are all correct as stated. All three statements hold. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: The Doldrums or Belt of Calms is associated with:
solution: The doldrums is the calm equatorial trough where the trade winds of the two hemispheres converge, which is precisely the ITCZ. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following cells of global atmospheric circulation was proposed by George Hadley in 1735?
solution: George Hadley proposed the tropical overturning cell in 1735 and it is named the Hadley cell after him. The Ferrel cell is named for William Ferrel and the Walker circulation for Gilbert Walker. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Geostrophic winds blow:
optA: Parallel to isobars when pressure gradient force balances Coriolis force
optB: Perpendicular to isobars due to friction dominance
optC: From low to high pressure due to gravitational force
optD: Along meridians unaffected by Earth's rotation
solution: Well above the friction layer the pressure gradient force and the Coriolis force come into balance, and the resulting geostrophic wind blows parallel to the isobars. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Semantic duplicate of bank row a1df50b6...

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following characteristics of upper-level winds:
1. Absent friction effect
2. Balance between pressure gradient force and Coriolis force
3. Flow parallel to isobars
Which of the above characteristics is/are true for geostrophic winds?
solution: Geostrophic flow is defined for the friction free upper air, arises from the balance of pressure gradient and Coriolis forces, and is directed along the isobars. All three characteristics are true. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of decreasing atmospheric pressure from surface to upper atmosphere?
solution: Pressure falls continuously with height, so the layers in order of decreasing pressure are simply the layers in order of increasing altitude. That is troposphere, then stratosphere, then mesosphere, then thermosphere. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Sea breeze blows during daytime because:
optA: Land cools faster than sea creating high pressure over land
optB: Sea heats faster than land creating low pressure over sea
optC: Land heats faster than sea creating low pressure over land
optD: Sea cools faster than land creating high pressure over sea
solution: Land has a much lower specific heat than water, so by day it heats faster and the air above it rises, creating low pressure over land. Air then moves inland from the sea as the sea breeze. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements about local winds:
1. Chinook is a warm downslope wind melting snow in Rocky Mountains.
2. Mistral is a cold katabatic wind flowing from Alps to Mediterranean.
3. Loo is a hot dry wind blowing in Northern Plains of India during summer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Chinook is the warm dry snow eater descending the eastern Rockies, Mistral is a cold wind draining from the Alps and adjoining highlands down to the Mediterranean, and Loo is the hot dry summer wind of the north Indian plains. All three statements are correct. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: The vertical decrease in atmospheric pressure follows approximately:
optA: 1 mb per 10 m elevation gain near sea level
optD: No regular pattern due to temperature variations
solution: Near sea level pressure falls by roughly one millibar for every ten metres of ascent, which is about 34 millibars per 300 metres. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following forces is responsible for deflecting winds to the right in Northern Hemisphere and left in Southern Hemisphere?
solution: The apparent deflecting force arising from the rotation of the earth is the Coriolis force, and it turns winds to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: Subpolar Low Pressure Belts (60°-65° N/S) experience stormy weather primarily because:
optA: Converging westerlies and polar easterlies create instability
optB: Sinking cold air from poles dominates
optC: Trade winds diverge creating low pressure
solution: At the subpolar low the warm moist westerlies meet the cold dense polar easterlies along the polar front, and the forced ascent of the warm air makes the zone unstable and cyclone prone. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: The instrument used for measuring atmospheric pressure is:
solution: A barometer, either the mercury type or the aneroid type, measures atmospheric pressure. A hygrometer measures humidity, a thermometer temperature and an anemometer wind speed. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Westerlies blow between:
solution: Westerlies flow polewards out of the subtropical high and into the subpolar low, that is between about 30 and 60 degrees. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Close spacing of isobars on a weather map indicates:
optA: Gentle pressure gradient and light winds
optB: Steep pressure gradient and strong winds
solution: Closely spaced isobars mean a large pressure change over a short distance, which is a steep pressure gradient, and the pressure gradient force then drives strong winds. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hydrostatic balance prevents strong upward winds despite large vertical pressure gradient.
2. Friction causes surface winds to cross isobars toward low pressure.
3. Planetary winds include Trade winds, Westerlies and Polar Easterlies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution: Hydrostatic balance holds the very large vertical pressure gradient against gravity so no strong vertical wind results, surface friction turns winds across the isobars towards low pressure, and the three planetary wind systems are the trades, the westerlies and the polar easterlies. All three statements are correct. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: The committee \(\underline{\text{will}}\) finalize the report next week.
solution: Here will carries the future tense of the main verb finalize and takes no object of its own. It is a modal auxiliary verb, not the noun meaning determination or a testament. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: She \(\underline{\text{can}}\) speak five languages fluently.
solution: Can expresses ability and is followed by the bare infinitive speak, which is the main verb. Can is therefore the modal auxiliary. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The sprinter ran \(\underline{\text{fast}}\) to win the race.
solution: Fast here modifies the verb ran, telling how the sprinter ran. A word qualifying a verb is an adverb. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The \(\underline{\text{fast}}\) train arrived on time.
solution: Fast here stands before the noun train and describes it. A word qualifying a noun is an adjective. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: He is poor \(\underline{\text{but}}\) honest.
solution: But joins the two contrasting complements poor and honest. A joining word of this kind is a conjunction. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The child \(\underline{\text{hurt}}\) his finger on the sharp edge.
solution: Hurt is the past tense finite verb whose subject is the child and whose object is his finger. It is therefore a verb. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: His \(\underline{\text{hurt}}\) expression touched everyone's heart.
solution: Hurt stands before the noun expression and describes it, giving the sense of a pained look. A word qualifying a noun is an adjective. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Hard \(\underline{\text{work}}\) always pays.
solution: Work is the subject of the verb pays and is itself qualified by the adjective hard. A word naming a thing and acting as subject is a noun. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Please \(\underline{\text{work}}\) hard to succeed.
solution: This is an imperative sentence in which work is the command, with hard modifying it as an adverb. Work is therefore the main verb. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The \(\underline{\text{old}}\) man walked slowly down the street.
solution: Old stands before the noun man and describes him. A word qualifying a noun is an adjective. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Semantic duplicate of bank row adbd0e95...

subject: English
stem: The earth revolves \(\underline{\text{round}}\) the sun.
solution: Round is followed by the noun the sun, which is its object, and it shows the relation between the revolving and the sun. A word governing a noun in this way is a preposition. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: He has a \(\underline{\text{round}}\) face.
solution: Round stands before the noun face and describes its shape, and it takes no object. It is therefore an adjective. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Jump \(\underline{\text{over}}\) the hurdle.
solution: Over takes the noun the hurdle as its object and shows the relation between the jumping and the hurdle. It is a preposition. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: The game is \(\underline{\text{over}}\).
solution: Over here has no object at all, and traditional Indian grammar treats a preposition used without an object as an adverb, which is the standard contrast drilled against Q73. The competing analysis is that over after the copula is a predicative adjective meaning finished, so both readings are defensible. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Contested: keyed Adverb per the traditional object-less-preposition convention this paper drills against Q73, and consistent with the bank keying 'knock that vase over' as Adverb. Modern descriptive grammar calls predicative 'over' an adjective (option C), which is also defensible.

subject: English
stem: The soldiers fought \(\underline{\text{bravely}}\).
solution: Bravely modifies the verb fought and tells how the soldiers fought. It is an adverb, and the ly ending confirms it. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: He is a \(\underline{\text{brave}}\) soldier.
solution: Brave stands before the noun soldier and describes him. A word qualifying a noun is an adjective. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: I know \(\underline{\text{that}}\) man.
solution: That here stands before the noun man and points it out, so its true label is demonstrative adjective or determiner, because it is not standing in place of a noun. The question is DEFECTIVE since no option offers adjective; demonstrative pronoun is the nearest of the four, as traditional books group the demonstratives together. Matches option A.
reviewNote: The correct class for 'that' before a noun is demonstrative adjective / determiner, which is NOT among the four options (the bank keys the same construction as 'Determiner'). Keyed to the nearest offered option.

subject: English
stem: I think \(\underline{\text{that}}\) he is right.
solution: That introduces the noun clause he is right, which is the object of think, and it replaces nothing inside that clause. A word linking a subordinate clause in this way is a conjunction. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: This is the house \(\underline{\text{that}}\) Jack built.
solution: That refers back to the noun house and at the same time serves as the object of built inside its own clause. Doing both jobs makes it a relative pronoun. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: \(\underline{\text{May}}\) I come in?
solution: May here asks permission and is followed by the bare infinitive come, so it is a modal auxiliary verb. It is not the noun naming the fifth month. Matches option B.
